title: 1 Timothy Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Timothy chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Timothy Chapter 6.

questions.question: In 1 Timothy 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Let servants count their own masters worthy of all honour
Godliness with contentment is great gain
If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words
Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds
questions.correctAnswer: Let servants count their own masters worthy of all honour
questions.explanation: This command appears first in 1 Timothy 6:1, which is the opening verse of the chapter.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6, how should servants regard their masters?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 instructs servants to count their own masters worthy of all honour.

questions.question: What reason is given for servants to honour their masters in 1 Timothy 6:1?
options: That the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed
So they will receive a reward
questions.correctAnswer: That the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed
questions.explanation: The verse states servants should honour their masters so that the name of God and his doctrine are not blasphemed.

questions.question: What are servants told to do if they have believing masters?
options: Not despise them because they are brethren
questions.correctAnswer: Not despise them because they are brethren
questions.explanation: Verse 2 instructs servants with believing masters not to despise them because they are brethren.

questions.question: Why should servants do service to believing masters according to 1 Timothy 6:2?
options: Because they are faithful and beloved
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are faithful and beloved
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says servants should serve believing masters because they are faithful and beloved.

questions.question: What should be done with those who teach otherwise and consent not to wholesome words?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 instructs to withdraw from men of corrupt minds who suppose that gain is godliness.

questions.question: What kind of words are described as wholesome in 1 Timothy 6:3?
options: The words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the doctrine according to godliness
questions.correctAnswer: The words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the doctrine according to godliness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 specifies wholesome words as those of Jesus Christ and godly doctrine.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:4, what negative emotions and conflicts come from pride and ignorance?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 lists envy, strife, railings, and evil surmisings as coming from prideful ignorance.

questions.question: What do men of corrupt minds suppose according to 1 Timothy 6:5?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states that such men suppose that gain is godliness.

questions.question: What is described as great gain in 1 Timothy 6?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 declares godliness with contentment is great gain.

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:7 say about what we bring into and carry out of this world?
options: We brought nothing into this world, and cannot carry anything out
We bring all our possessions in and out
We bring our knowledge in and out
We bring our family in and out
questions.correctAnswer: We brought nothing into this world, and cannot carry anything out
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that we brought nothing into this world and cannot carry anything out.

questions.question: Who should servants especially honour according to 1 Timothy 6?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 commands servants to honour their own masters.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Timothy 6 teaches that servants should not despise believing masters because they are brethren.
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states servants with believing masters should not despise them because they are brethren.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Timothy 6 says godliness with contentment is great gain.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 clearly states that godliness with contentment is great gain.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Timothy 6 teaches that gain is the same as godliness.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says men of corrupt minds suppose gain is godliness, implying it is not true.

medium.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Timothy Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should we be content with according to 1 Timothy 6:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:8 states, 'And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:9 promise will happen if someone desires to be rich?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:9 warns that 'they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare.'

questions.question: What is described as the root of all evil in 1 Timothy 6:10?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:10 states, 'For the love of money is the root of all evil.'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:11, what should a man of God flee from?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:11 instructs to 'flee these things' referring to the temptation and lusts of money.

questions.question: What are the qualities that 1 Timothy 6:11 encourages us to pursue?
options: Righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:11 lists these qualities to pursue.

questions.question: In 1 Timothy 6:12, what does Paul encourage Timothy to fight?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:12 states, 'Fight the good fight of faith.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:13 emphasize about Christ Jesus?
options: He is the judge of all
He witnessed a good confession before Pontius Pilate
He is the source of all wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: He witnessed a good confession before Pontius Pilate
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:13 mentions this specific testimony of Christ.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:14, what should Timothy keep without spot?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:14 instructs to 'keep this commandment without spot.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:6 say is great gain?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:6 states, 'But godliness with contentment is great gain.'

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in 1 Timothy 6:10 for those who covet after money?
options: They have erred from the faith
questions.correctAnswer: They have erred from the faith
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:10 states, 'which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith.'

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:7, what did we bring into this world?
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:7 states, 'For we brought nothing into this world.'

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:5 warn us to withdraw from?
options: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds
questions.correctAnswer: Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:5 advises to withdraw from such individuals.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Timothy 6:8, contentment is linked with having food and raiment.
questions.explanation: This is correct as 1 Timothy 6:8 states, 'And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.'

questions.question: True or False: 1 Timothy 6:10 says that money itself is the root of all evil.
questions.explanation: This is correct because 1 Timothy 6:10 specifies that 'the love of money is the root of all evil,' not money itself.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Timothy 6:14, Timothy should keep the commandment unrebukeable until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect; 1 Timothy 6:14 indeed states that Timothy should keep the commandment unrebukeable until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

hard.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Timothy Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:15, who is described as the 'blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords'?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:15 identifies 'the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords' as the one who shall show himself in his times, referring to Jesus Christ's sovereign authority.

questions.question: In 1 Timothy 6:16, what unique attribute is given to God regarding immortality?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:16 explicitly states that God 'only hath immortality,' emphasizing the uniqueness of God's eternal nature.

questions.question: What does 1 Timothy 6:17 instruct the rich not to trust in?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:17 advises the rich to not be highminded or trust in 'uncertain riches,' but rather in the living God.

questions.question: According to 1 Timothy 6:18, the rich are encouraged to be rich in what?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:18 commands the rich to be 'rich in good works,' ready to distribute and willing to communicate.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'laying up in store for themselves a good foundation' according to 1 Timothy 6:19?
options: To lay hold on eternal life
questions.correctAnswer: To lay hold on eternal life
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:19 explains that laying up a good foundation is to prepare for the time to come so that they may 'lay hold on eternal life.'

questions.question: In 1 Timothy 6:20, what is Timothy specifically instructed to avoid?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:20 commands Timothy to keep the entrusted teachings and avoid 'profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called.'

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'Potentate' (ἐξουσιαστής) in 1 Timothy 6:15?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'Potentate' (ἐξουσιαστής) in 1 Timothy 6:15 means 'ruler with supreme authority,' fitting the description of God as sovereign King.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Timothy 6:15 with the titles 'King of kings, and Lord of lords'?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:15 uses 'King of kings, and Lord of lords' as a form of superlative intensification, emphasizing God's supreme sovereignty over all.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with 1 Timothy 6:16's description of God dwelling in unapproachable light?
questions.explanation: Exodus 33:20 states 'No man shall see me, and live,' connecting directly with 1 Timothy 6:16's description of God dwelling in unapproachable light.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the warning in 1 Timothy 6:10 about the 'love of money' being the root of all evil?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:5 warns not to love money and be content with what you have, echoing 1 Timothy 6:10's warning that the love of money is the root of all evil.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 1 Timothy 6:15 in the chapter?
options: The command to keep the commandment without spot until Christ's appearing
The instruction to fight the good fight of faith
The charge to flee from foolish lusts
The exhortation to be content with food and raiment
questions.correctAnswer: The command to keep the commandment without spot until Christ's appearing
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:14 commands to keep the commandment without spot until the appearing of Christ, which immediately precedes verse 15.

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 6:6 relate godliness to contentment, and what literary figure does this illustrate?
options: It presents a parallelism illustrating that godliness with contentment is great gain
It uses metaphor to compare godliness to money
It employs irony to criticize materialism
It uses allegory to depict spiritual wealth
questions.correctAnswer: It presents a parallelism illustrating that godliness with contentment is great gain
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:6 states 'godliness with contentment is great gain,' illustrating a parallelism between spiritual piety and satisfaction as a literary device.

questions.question: Which phrase in 1 Timothy 6:20 refers to 'science falsely so called' and what is its Greek term?
options: 'Oppositions of science falsely so called' – Greek: 'antitheseis tēs pseudomathias'
questions.correctAnswer: 'Oppositions of science falsely so called' – Greek: 'antitheseis tēs pseudomathias'
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:20 uses the phrase 'oppositions of science falsely so called,' from the Greek 'antitheseis tēs pseudomathias,' referring to false knowledge or teachings.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the phrase 'to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.' in 1 Timothy 6:16?
options: It serves as a doxology affirming God's eternal glory and authority
It is a benediction directed to Timothy
It denotes the completion of the law
It is a prophetic declaration of the Messiah's coming
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as a doxology affirming God's eternal glory and authority
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:16 ends with a doxology, 'to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen,' affirming God's eternal glory and sovereign authority.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Timothy 6:7, it is certain that we can carry nothing out of this world.
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:7 explicitly states 'For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.'

theological.title: 1 Timothy Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Timothy Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Timothy 6:6 teach about godliness and contentment?
options: Godliness with contentment is great gain
Godliness is sufficient for salvation without contentment
Contentment comes only after perfect sanctification
Contentment is a result of wealth and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Godliness with contentment is great gain
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:6 teaches that godliness combined with contentment constitutes great gain, emphasizing a spiritual posture rather than material wealth.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Timothy 6:3 teach about the proper teaching of Christian doctrine?
options: Wholesome words align with the doctrine according to godliness
Any teaching that promotes debate is acceptable
Doctrine is flexible according to cultural context
Faithful teaching excludes the words of Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Wholesome words align with the doctrine according to godliness
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:3 states that teaching must consent to wholesome words and doctrine according to godliness, linking proper doctrine directly to godly living.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the love of money is taught in 1 Timothy 6:10?
options: The love of money is the root of all evil
Money itself is evil and to be shunned
Wealth is a sign of God's approval
questions.correctAnswer: The love of money is the root of all evil
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:10 clearly teaches that it is the love of money, not money itself, that is the root of all evil, causing some to stray from faith.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Timothy 6:16 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:16 speaks of God as the only one who has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, demonstrating the divine attribute of immortality.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Timothy 6:13 regarding God's oversight?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:13 charges Timothy in the sight of God and Christ Jesus, indicating God's sovereign authority and oversight over all things.

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 6:12 prepare for the New Testament theme of perseverance in salvation?
options: By exhorting to fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life
By promising immediate relief from trials
By suggesting salvation is guaranteed irrespective of faith
questions.correctAnswer: By exhorting to fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:12 connects with the New Testament theme of persevering in faith to attain eternal life, highlighting active spiritual struggle.

questions.question: In what way does 1 Timothy 6:17–19 connect to the broader biblical teaching on stewardship and eternal rewards?
options: By commanding the rich to do good and lay up a good foundation for the time to come
By promising riches as a sign of God's blessing
By advising accumulation of wealth for security
By teaching wealth is irrelevant to Christian conduct
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding the rich to do good and lay up a good foundation for the time to come
questions.explanation: These verses teach that the wealthy should use resources for good works, accumulating treasures in heaven, aligning with biblical stewardship principles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Timothy 6:9 and 1 Timothy 6:10 teach about wealth and temptation?
options: The desire for riches leads to temptation and many harmful lusts, causing destruction
Wealth guarantees spiritual security and blessing
All riches are inherently sinful and to be rejected
Temptation comes only from poverty, not wealth
questions.correctAnswer: The desire for riches leads to temptation and many harmful lusts, causing destruction
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 connect the desire for riches with falling into temptation and harmful passions, teaching the spiritual dangers of covetousness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Timothy 6:20 and 1 Timothy 6:21 teach about false knowledge and faith?
options: Timothy is to avoid profane babblings and oppositions of falsely called knowledge that cause errors concerning faith
All knowledge is beneficial for faith development
False knowledge is acceptable if it promotes unity
Faith can be maintained alongside profane babblings
questions.correctAnswer: Timothy is to avoid profane babblings and oppositions of falsely called knowledge that cause errors concerning faith
questions.explanation: These verses warn Timothy to guard the faith by rejecting false teachings labeled as knowledge, which lead to errors about the faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Timothy 6:1 and 1 Timothy 6:2 teach about social relations and Christian conduct?
options: Servants must honor their masters to avoid blasphemy of God’s name, even if the masters are believers
Servants can disregard masters who are not believers
Christian love removes all social distinctions without obligation
Masters and servants are equal in social status
questions.correctAnswer: Servants must honor their masters to avoid blasphemy of God’s name, even if the masters are believers
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 2 instruct servants to honor their masters, including believing ones, so that God’s name and doctrine are not blasphemed, showing Christian ethics in social roles.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Timothy 6:3-5 encourages intellectual arrogance and divisive arguments. What does 1 Timothy 6:3-5 actually teach?
options: It warns against proud, ignorant disputers promoting false doctrine and greed, urging withdrawal from them
It encourages constant debate to refine doctrine
It accepts all opinions as equally valid
It claims that gain is godliness
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against proud, ignorant disputers promoting false doctrine and greed, urging withdrawal from them
questions.explanation: These verses warn that those who reject wholesome doctrine and promote quarrels about gain are corrupt and to be avoided, opposing arrogance in teaching.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian virtues is taught in 1 Timothy 6:11?
options: A man of God should flee evil desires and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, and meekness
Christian virtues are optional and cultural
Patience and meekness are unimportant compared to knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: A man of God should flee evil desires and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, and meekness
questions.explanation: Verse 11 calls believers to actively pursue a list of virtues as integral to godly living, which is essential for sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding human possession and mortality is taught in 1 Timothy 6:7?
options: We brought nothing into the world and cannot carry anything out
Possessions guarantee security in life and after death
Eternal life depends on earthly wealth
Material gains are evidence of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: We brought nothing into the world and cannot carry anything out
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 6:7 teaches the doctrine of human mortality and the temporary nature of material possessions, emphasizing spiritual priorities.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 1 Timothy 6:15 when describing Christ’s future appearing?
options: Sovereignty as King of kings and Lord of lords
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty as King of kings and Lord of lords
questions.explanation: Verse 15 refers to Christ’s future appearing as the blessed and only Potentate, King of kings, and Lord of lords, highlighting divine sovereignty.

questions.question: How does 1 Timothy 6:8 contribute to biblical teaching on contentment and sufficiency?
options: Having food and raiment, let us be content, emphasizing sufficiency in basic needs
We must seek abundance beyond basic needs to prove faith
Contentment is only attainable through wealth
Sufficiency is irrelevant to spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Having food and raiment, let us be content, emphasizing sufficiency in basic needs
questions.explanation: Verse 8 teaches contentment with having basic necessities, reinforcing biblical themes of trusting God for provision rather than craving excess.
